newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank hands-off on currency - Sheu.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank hands-off on currency - Sheu.

text.p: Taiwan central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on Thursday the bank found current Taiwan dollar levels tolerable and would not intervene in the foreign exchange market unless local industry were affected.
"The Taiwan dollar exchange rate is still tolerable," Sheu told parliament. "In the future, we will intervene in the foreign exchange only if there is an influence on industry."

The Taiwan dollar, which gained slightly against the U.S. dollar on Wednesday to close at T$27.520, has depreciated only slightly against the U.S. dollar during the greenback's two year rise, while appreciating against the yen and deutsche mark.
The Taiwan dollar's stubbornly high levels has prompted some Taiwan exporters and economists to say it was overvalued.
Sheu said the strong Taiwan dollar was helping importers.
"The current (Taiwan dollar) levels will not hurt our industrial competitiveness because it is cheaper now to import raw materials and components from Japan," Sheu said.

The central bank tried briefly in mid-1996 to engineer a depreciation to help the exporters, a crucial sector of Taiwan's economy, but the currency rebounded within weeks to its longstanding level of around T$27.5 to the dollar.
The Taiwan dollar opened slightly lower against the U.S. dollar on Thursday, and was trading at T$27.527 at midmorning while Sheu was still speaking.
